AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 13.04.2018 PASSED IN MVC NO.302/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS AND MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, BYADAGI, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
S.R.KRISHNA KUMAR, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -5-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:10869-DB  MFA No. 102573 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 102714 of 2018  JUDGMENT Both these appeals arise out of the impugned judgment and award dated 13.04.2018 passed in M.V.C. No.302/2016 by the Senior Civil judge & JMFC, and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Byadgi (for short, 'the Tribunal').
2. Heard the learned counsel for the claimants and the learned counsel for the insurance company,
and perused the material on record.
3. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to as per their rankings before the Tribunal.
4. The material on record discloses that the claimants are the parents and the unmarried sister of the late S.S.Shivakumar who died in a fatal road traffic accident that occurred on 31.12.2015.

In the said claim petition, the claimants specifically contended that when the aforesaid late The Divisional Manager vs Sri S.P. Sattyanarayana S/O ... on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169646507/
4 S.S.Shivakumar and his friends were traveling in Hyundai Verna car bearing registration No.KA- NC: 2023:KHC-D:10869-DB 51/MG-7125, due to rash and negligent driving of the car by its driver,
the car met with an accident resulting in the demise of the aforesaid S.S.Shivakumar.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was also contended that the deceased was working as an Assistant Manager in a private finance company and was earning Rs.22,000/- per month; they were dependent on the income of the deceased for their livelihood; and respondent No.1 being the owner of the said car and respondent No.2 being the insurer were jointly and severally liable to pay compensation in favour of the claimants.
5.
Respondent No.1, owner-cum-driver of the car, filed his statement of objections disputing the averments made in the claim petition and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

In the alternative, respondent No.1 stated that in the event compensation is ordered to be paid in favour of the claimants, respondent No.2-insuance company was to be fastened with the liability to pay compensation.

Respondent No.2-insurance company also filed its separate statement of objections inter alia contending that the accident in question occurred when respondent No.1 was using the car for commercial use and as such, respondent No.2 was not liable to indemnify respondent No.1.

It was also contended that the deceased S.S.Shivakumar was not wearing seat belt at the time of the accident which resulted in his demise and consequently, the question of respondent No.2 paying any compensation did not arise in the facts and circumstances of the case.
It was further contended that there was no merit in the claim petition and the same is liable to be dismissed.

7. After trial, during which the claimant No.1 examined himself as P.W.1 and Exs.P.1 to P.24 were marked; respondent No.2 examined its Manager as R.W.1 and Exs.R1 to R2 were marked, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident in question was on account of the rash and negligent driving of the car by respondent NC: 2023:KHC-D:10869-DB No.1 - owner & driver of the car and consequently, respondent No.2 being the insurer was liable to pay compensation in favour of the claimant.
8.

Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal accepted the contention of the claimants that the deceased was working in a private finance company and was earning Rs.22,000/- per month and consequently awarded compensation under various heads in favour of the claimants together with interest at 7% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
9. Aggrieved by the liability as well as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal,
respondent
No.2 -
insurance
company has preferred the appeal M.F.A. No.102573/2018, while the claimants have also preferred an appeal in M.F.A. No.102714/2018 aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: 5 10. A perusal of the material on record will indicate that though insurance company has taken up a specific contention that the accident in question resulted in the demise of late S.S.Shivakumar since he was not wearing the seat belt due to which the Air Bags did not open up, except the said bald plea taken in the statement of objections, the insurance company has not adduced any legal or acceptable evidence to establish thus contention; in other words, except stating that if the deceased S.S.Shivakumar had worn the seat belt, the Air Bags would have opened up at the time of the accident and aforesaid S.S.Shivakumar would not have expired in the same, respondent No.2 has not examined any person either from Hyundai Company or any other technical expert so as to establish that the demise of S.S.Shivakumar was on account of non-opening of the Air Bags due to non-wearing of the seat belt.

It is needless to state that mere violation of Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, and Rule 230 of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, which mandate wearing of seat belt,
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10869-DB cannot be made the basis to come to the conclusion that the demise of the foresaid S.S.Shivakumar was not to due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1, the owner-cum-driver of the offending car.
Under these circumstances, we are of the considered opinion that the Tribunal was fully justified in rejecting the said contention urged on behalf of the insurance company.

11. Insofar as the contention urged by the insurance company that the author of the documents viz.,
the appointment letter, salary certificates, increments certificate issued on behalf of M/s. Antrax Technologies Pvt Ltd., the company in which S.S.Shivakumar ws working, has not been examined is concerned, a perusal of the material on record comprising of the appointment letter of S.S.Shivakumar at Ex.P.9, Bank Passbooks at Exs.P.10 & P.11, Certificate of appreciation at Ex.P.14,
and salary increment letters Exs.P.15 to P.17, as well as Degree Certificate, which indicates that he has passed B.Com., course, and the Identity Card of S.S.Shivakumar marked - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10869-DB as Ex.P.20, cumulatively establish that S.S.Shivakumar was working at Antrax Technologies Pvt. Ltd earning Rs.20,000/- to Rs.22,000/- per month.

Under these circumstances, in the absence of any contra/rebuttal evidence adduced by the insurance company to establish that S.S.Shivakumar was not working at M/s. Antrax Technologies Pvt. Ltd., or he was employed somewhere else or that he was not at all employed, we are of the view that the Tribunal was justified in coming to the conclusion that the deceased S.S.Shivakumar had income of Rs.22,000/- per month and consequently, the claimants were entitled to compensation towards loss of dependency.

12. Insofar as compensation under other heads is concerned, bearing in mind the judgments of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another1,
National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi2, and Magma General Insurance (2009)6 SCC 121 (2017)16 SCC 680 The Divisional Manager vs Sri S.P. Sattyanarayana S/O ... on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169646507/
6 - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10869-DB Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram & Ors.3, we deem it just and appropriate to allow/dispose of both the appeals and modify the impugned judgment and award and grant just and fair compensation by reassessing the compensation towards loss of consortium and by reducing the interest from 7% per annum to 6% per annum as under:
1) Loss of dependency Rs. 34,47,198/-
2) Loss consortium to claimants Rs. 1,20,000/-
 3) Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
 4) Towards funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-
 Total Rs. 35,97,198/-
Thus, the appellants-claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.35,97,198/- as against Rs.35,40,198/-
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

2018 ACJ 2782 - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10869-DB ORDER i) Both the appeals are partly allowed.
ii) The impugned judgment and award, dated 13.04.2018, passed in M.V.C.
No.302/2016 by the Tribunal dismissing the claim petition is modified.

iii) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.35,97,198/- as against Rs.35,40,198/-
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
iv) The respondent No.2-insurance company shall deposit the aforesaid compensation along with interest within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
v) The apportionment of compensation and deposit and release of the same shall be as per the order of the Tribunal .

A perusal of the material on record will indicate that though insurance company has taken up a specific contention that the accident in question resulted in the demise of late S.S.Shivakumar since he was not wearing the seat belt due to which the Air Bags did not open up, except the said bald plea taken in the statement of objections, the insurance company has not adduced any legal or acceptable evidence to establish thus contention; in other words, except stating that if the deceased S.S.Shivakumar had worn the seat belt, the Air Bags would have opened up at the time of the accident and aforesaid S.S.Shivakumar would not have expired in the same, respondent No.2 has not examined any person either from Hyundai Company or any other technical expert so as to establish that the demise of S.S.Shivakumar was on account of non-opening of the Air Bags due to non-wearing of the seat belt.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is needless to state that mere violation of Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, and Rule 230 of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, which mandate wearing of seat belt,
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10869-DB cannot be made the basis to come to the conclusion that the demise of the foresaid S.S.Shivakumar was not to due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1, the owner-cum-driver of the offending car.
Under these circumstances, in the absence of any contra/rebuttal evidence adduced by the insurance company to establish that S.S.Shivakumar was not working at M/s. Antrax Technologies Pvt. Ltd., or he was employed somewhere else or that he was not at all employed, we are of the view that the Tribunal was justified in coming to the conclusion that the deceased S.S.Shivakumar had income of Rs.22,000/- per month and consequently, the claimants were entitled to compensation towards loss of dependency.
opennyai_summary.decision:
13. In the result, we pass the following:
2018 ACJ 2782 - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10869-DB ORDER i) Both the appeals are partly allowed.
ii) The impugned judgment and award, dated 13.04.2018, passed in M.V.C.
No.302/2016 by the Tribunal dismissing the claim petition is modified.
iii) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.35,97,198/- as against Rs.35,40,198/-
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
iv) The respondent No.2-insurance company shall deposit the aforesaid compensation along with interest within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
v) The apportionment of compensation and deposit and release of the same shall be as per the order of the Tribunal .
